name: LiliPUT
label: Rough Trade
lede: Two Zurich artists learned their instruments in a bunker, got a guitarist at their first encore, and were famous enough in Britain by 1979 for Kleenex's lawyers to come calling.

eras.title: Learning to play in a Zurich bunker
eras.text: Lislot Ha and Klaudia Schiff were a two-woman art act making short films when Zurich's punk scene pulled them into music. Within the year they had a guitarist, a self-paid record and a slot on Swiss TV.

years.h: Ha, Schiff and Regula Sing start Kleenex in a bunker
years.p: Drummer Ha and bassist Schiff, an art duo called Superchunks since 1977, start the band with singer Sing and learn their instruments in a Zurich bunker. Two members of the Nasal Boys help out on guitar.

years.src: New York Times · Wikipedia (de): Kleenex · Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder
years.h: Marlene Marder joins the band during the encore
years.p: Kleenex open for the Nasal Boys at Club Hey, Zurich, at 10:30 p.m. with four songs. The crowd wants more, the stand-in guitarist won't go back out, and Marder, who'd learned the songs, plays them all again.
years.xp:
Marder had been playing saxophone in Zurich's punk scene and met the band at a Nasal Boys show a few weeks earlier. The four songs were 'Beri-Beri', 'Ain't You', 'Hedi's Head' and 'Nice', she told Perfect Sound Forever.

A month later Kleenex opened for [[XTC|97c86b2c-2765-46a2-aef8-76a7e24c430f]] at the Limmathaus, and from May 3 they played as a four-woman band, which became their image in the press whether they liked it or not.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder · Wikipedia (de): Kleenex
years.h: Friends on the Sunrise label put out the first four songs
years.p: Two days at Sunrise's studio in Kirchberg in September produce a four-song single the band pays for itself. Sounds makes it Single of the Week.
years.xp: "They thought it was it would be nice to do a single and that was it," Marder said of the friends behind it. The sleeve and press photos had critics reaching for Dada, Expressionism and Futurism, a connection [[Greil Marcus|9d3889fb-c6b7-47a8-a325-d22ea54292e3]] picked up later.

years.h: A Swiss TV mime costs Regula Sing her day job
years.p: The teatime show Karussell lets Kleenex mime only, to the band's disgust. After it airs, Sing loses her job as a sales assistant at a Zurich photo shop.

eras.title: Peel, the Raincoats and a letter from Kimberly-Clark
eras.text: A friend carried the Sunrise record to England and John Peel did the rest. Rough Trade signed the band, sent it on tour with the Raincoats, and by November the tissue company wanted its name back.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder · Wikipedia (de): Kleenex · Wikipedia: LiLiPUT
years.h: John Peel plays the Swiss EP until Rough Trade signs them
years.p: Peel plays it over and over; [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]] signs the band and issues 'Ain't You' / 'Hedi's Head' in Britain. By April it has sold 12,000 copies.
years.xp: "John Peel got the EP and he played it on the radio over and over. Rough Trade heard it and that was the contact," Marder said.

years.cap: The band photo printed as a puzzle inside the 'You' / 'Ü' sleeve, 1979
years.src: Wikipedia (de): Kleenex · Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder
years.h: 'You' comes out as the UK tour with the Raincoats begins
years.p: Recorded in six days at Kingsway Studios, London, the single 'You' / 'Ü' lands on the first day of a tour with [[The Raincoats|42201355-08b7-43b6-a7b8-866f612e1600]] and Spizzenergi that runs to June 5.
years.xp: "The audience was GREAT. I was suprised," Marder said. She stayed friends with the Raincoats, and with [[Mayo Thompson|b463f760-e381-462a-b060-78606b78e5e1]] of Red Krayola.

years.h: The tour ends Kleenex's first line-up, and their gear goes back
years.p: The band parts ways with Sing by mutual agreement after long-running differences. The tour made no money, and the manager had missed equipment payments, so amps and instruments had to be returned.

years.h: Chrigle Freund, 16, takes the train from Bern three times a week
years.p: Formerly of Bern punks Chaos, Freund wins the singer's job and eventually moves into Schiff's house. Saxophonist Angie Barrack joins in December.

years.big: A new name, or the records get destroyed.
q: We had to pay thousands of Swiss francs for this.
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder · Wikipedia (de): Kleenex
years.h: Kimberly-Clark's lawyers write to Klaudia Schiff
years.p: The owner of the Kleenex trademark bars the band from using the name. Marder said the company threatened to have Rough Trade destroy all the records.
years.xp: "They said we had to change our name or otherwise they will call Rough Trade to destroy all the records," Marder told Perfect Sound Forever. The band also had to pay.

eras.title: Dada costumes and a mountain of debt
eras.text: The new name came from Lislot Ha, and the new sound was messier. Two singles made the UK indie charts and Greil Marcus wrote them into his books, while the band went through two drummers, two saxophonists and a singer.

years.h: 'Split' is the first LiliPUT single
years.p: Cut at Sunrise in Kirchberg and released by Rough Trade, it's far more chaotic than Kleenex. The partly whistled B-side 'Die Matrosen' helps it into the UK indie chart.
years.xp: The new name took a while. The line-up's first show, in Geneva on April 2, went out as Wigwam; on April 26 at Drahtschmidli, Zurich, they used Lislot Ha's suggestion, LiliPUT, for the first time.

years.h: A week in England ends with Lislot Ha quitting
years.p: Another tour ends in a row, and the co-founder leaves music altogether, as does Barrack. A German tour booked for November is cancelled.

years.h: The band dresses as Hugo Ball for the 'Eisiger Wind' sleeve
years.p: Recorded as a trio with Freund on drums and issued by Off Course in Switzerland and Rough Trade in Britain. The Dada costumes catch [[Greil Marcus|9d3889fb-c6b7-47a8-a325-d22ea54292e3]], whose essay on the band runs in New West that April.
years.xp: By release day Freund had left too, leaving Marder and Schiff as a duo. Schiff told an interviewer the band was sitting on a huge mountain of debt.

years.h: Astrid Spirig, an office worker from the band Neon, takes the mic
years.p: Spirig, 26, joins with drummer Beat Schlatter and saxophonist Christoph Herzog. Two men in the band puzzled the music press; the new line-up debuts at the Munich Rocktage in April.
years.xp: Marder's answer to the press, in German at the time: the band had never seen itself as a women's band and didn't want the media to sell it as one.

eras.title: Two albums and a pregnancy
eras.text: Rough Trade finally paid for an album, and the trio of Marder, Schiff and Spirig made two. Schiff was exhibiting at documenta, Marder was tired, and Spirig kept the band going until she couldn't.

years.h: Rough Trade pays for the first LiliPUT album
years.p: Recorded in February at Studio Platinum in Oberehrendingen with engineer Harry Zindel. The sound has moved toward loose, jazzy, improvised new wave.
years.xp:
Asked why it took four years, Marder said the band had paid for the singles themselves and an album cost far more: Rough Trade asked, and paid, so they did it.

A long German tour followed in September with Stephan Eicher as a guest; the band took a Super 8 camera and shot silent footage that surfaced on DVD in 2010.

years.h: Schiff and Marder want out; Spirig becomes the manager
years.p: Schiff had been showing her art at documenta in Kassel since June. After the tour she and Marder planned to end the band, until Spirig talked them round and took over the management.

q: She wanted to be 100% for the baby.
years.src: Wikipedia (de): Kleenex · Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder · Wikipedia: LiLiPUT
years.h: Some Songs comes out with no band to tour it
years.p: Spirig's news, as Marder remembered it, after Rough Trade Deutschland had funded the album to be toured. The trio had played its last show at the Mascotte in Zurich in October.
years.xp:
Spirig had negotiated the album money herself, after the band's March single 'The Jatz' / 'You Did It' became the new German label's first release. Marder recalled her asking them not to tell the label, which had put in all the money; Marder said she wasn't really disappointed, it was simply over.

Spirig had been planning to study at a musical school in New York, and later said she had to choose between New York and the child.

eras.title: The tapes in Marder's keeping
eras.text: Marder was the one who stayed in music, and the one who kept the tapes. Her compilation put the band back in print just as fans like Kurt Cobain were naming it.

years.cap: Marlene Marder backstage at the Rote Fabrik, Zurich
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever: Marlene Marder · New York Times
years.h: Marder publishes her diary of the band
years.p: The Diary of the Guitarist Marlene Marder, Kleenex/LiLiPUT collects her diary with interviews, press, photos and fan letters, 230 pages.

years.h: Off Course collects everything on two CDs
years.p: Marder pulls tracks from her own tapes and Schiff designs the cover. Greil Marcus writes the liner notes.
years.xp: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] listed "anything by Kleenex" among his 50 favourite albums. Kill Rock Stars reissued the set in the US in 2001, and Mississippi Records put it out as a four-LP box in 2011.

years.h: The TV clips, the road movie and the first songs come back
years.p: Kill Rock Stars' Live Recordings, TV-Clips & Roadmovie gathers the TV mimes, the 1983 Rote Fabrik show and the Super 8 tour footage. First Songs, the Kleenex singles on double LP, follows in 2016.

years.h: Marlene Marder dies at 61
years.p: Kill Rock Stars announced the death without giving a cause; German Wikipedia says cancer. After the band she ran a record shop and a booking agency and worked for the World Wide Fund for Nature.
years.xp: From 1989 to 1992 she played weekends in a hard-rock band, Danger Mice. Schiff, as Klaudia Schifferle, is a visual artist; Schlatter became a comedian on Swiss TV and film.
